title: Master's CI made honestly green — three failures fixed as real rot, one needs_houdini marker that provably hides nothing
ruling: HONESTY OVER A GREEN BADGE (Joe, as CTO). A green check that hides failures is worse than an honest red one.
status_note: Describes what happened (Law 3). On Python 3.14 the oracle is fully met: `pytest tests/ -m "not needs_houdini"` is 0-failed / 5682-passed in a CI-faithful clone with no pxr and no hou, and the unfiltered run has the SAME 5682 passes. On Python 3.11 the three target failures are fixed, but three OTHER tests fail — and they fail identically at the base commit, on Windows only, because they assert `elapsed > 0` against a clock with ~15.6 ms granularity. Both 3.11 legs passed on the last completed green CI run (30772612918, ubuntu + macos), which is the platform CI actually runs, so they are reported rather than fixed: fixing them means changing product timing code, which is a separate judgement (for_ruling #3). Nothing was weakened, xfailed, deleted or marked needs_houdini to reach this. Not merged, not pushed — Gate C is human.

the_three_failures.which_side_was_stale: THE MODULE WAS RETIRED DELIBERATELY; THE TEST AND ONE PRODUCTION CONSUMER WERE THE STALE SIDE.
evidence: VERIFIED-STATIC: commit 7f7bbc39 ('feat(moneta): production harness') renamed python/synapse/memory/evolution.py -> evolution.py.deprecated. Its own commit body says 'Remove evolution.py (-> evolution.py.deprecated)'.
VERIFIED-STATIC: docs/DEBUT_READINESS.md:120 documents the rename as intentional; docs/moneta-deep-review-2026-08-05.md:244 (B-S12) had already classified the module as dormant dead code.

VERIFIED-STATIC: tests/test_scene_memory.py:542 was ALREADY adapted to the retirement — it carries `skipif(not _EVO_AVAILABLE, reason='evolution.py not found (deprecated)')`. Two other call sites were missed.

VERIFIED-STATIC: python/synapse/server/handlers_memory.py:321 (pre-fix) still did `from ..memory.evolution import check_evolution, evolve_to_charmeleon` — so `_handle_evolve_memory` raised ImportError on EVERY invocation. The `evolve_memory` command and the `synapse_evolve_memory` MCP tool were dead on arrival and no test covered it.
the_three_failures.disposition: FIXED, not skipped. (a) handlers_memory._handle_evolve_memory rerouted to shared/evolution.py::LosslessEvolution + check_evolution_triggers — a strict superset of the retired evolver (same markdown->USD conversion, plus lossless verify with rollback, an immutable pre-evolution archive, and R10 viewport sync). Stage names match on both sides: shared/constants.py:298 defines EVOLUTION_STAGE_FLAT='charmander', _STRUCTURED='charmeleon', so the reply keys keep their old shape. The import is guarded and an unavailable `shared/` returns status 'unavailable', never a fake success (Law 3). (b) The test now asserts the retirement itself, in two halves: the module is gone from the tree, and NO shipped module imports the retired name.
the_three_failures.law_1_proof: The offender-scan half was PROVEN able to fail: run against `git show HEAD:python/synapse/server/handlers_memory.py`, the pattern hits line 321. The first pattern written did NOT hit it — `\bevolution\b` never matches inside `check_evolution` because `_` is a word character — so the check was toothless and was rewritten to anchor on the MODULE PATH. Positive controls (4 import shapes) and negative controls (shared.evolution, evolution_stage, scene_memory, a commented-out import) were run before the test was trusted.

the_three_failures.verdict_class: NOT ENVIRONMENTAL. The brief's triage is corrected here, with a probe.
the_three_failures.symptom: AssertionError: hard exit unexpectedly persisted — the durability of the clean-exit test cannot be attributed to atexit (assert 1 == 0)
the_three_failures.why_the_brief_class_is_refuted: REFUTED-LIVE: the test fails identically on an interpreter WHERE pxr IS PRESENT (system Python 3.14 with usd-core installed): `1 failed, 1 passed`. The pxr ModuleNotFoundError in the CI log is an incidental warning from moneta_store.py:282 falling back off USD sublayers; it is not the cause. The test therefore did NOT earn the needs_houdini marker, and marking it would have been the exact lie the ruling forbids.
the_three_failures.root_cause: python/synapse/memory/moneta_store.py:205 — `self._last_save: float = 0.0`. add() then checks `now - self._last_save >= self._save_interval` at :379 with `now = time.monotonic()`, which on any process is far above 30.0. So the check is ALWAYS true on the first deposit: the very first add() force-saves, synchronously, every time.

probe.producer: scratch probe, subprocess deposit -> count rows in .moneta/snapshot.json, moneta v1.2.0-rc3
probe.second_probe: with `_last_save = time.monotonic()` patched in, the 1-deposit hard exit persists 0 rows — i.e. the ORIGINAL assertions pass verbatim under that one-line change.

the_three_failures.the_finding_underneath: This is Law 1 in the flesh, and the negative control caught it exactly as designed. At 1 deposit the POSITIVE control (test_atexit_snapshots_deposits_on_clean_exit) was passing for the wrong reason — persistence came from the first-add save, not from the atexit hook it claimed to prove. The entire Phase-1 durability fix was unproven. Corroborating evidence that `_last_save = 0.0` is an anomaly and not a design: two other tests in the same file (lines 292, 336) have to reset `_last_save = time.monotonic()` by hand to make the timer testable, and one says so in its docstring.
the_three_failures.disposition: FIXED IN THE TESTS, NOT IN THE PRODUCT — deliberately. Both controls now deposit 3 memories: clean exit must persist 3 (proving atexit carried #2 and #3), hard exit must persist exactly 1 (proving nothing incidental covers #2 and #3, and that the first-add save is still firing). Both assertions are STRONGER than before — the old pair pinned one number between them, the new pair pins the boundary from both sides — so Law 6 holds. Production durability is deliberately NOT changed by a CI leg: the one-line `_last_save = time.monotonic()` alternative REDUCES first-deposit durability, and that is a posture judgement, escalated as for_ruling #1 rather than taken here.
the_three_failures.test_count: 2 tests before, 2 tests after. One renamed, because the old name asserted a total loss that never happens.

marker_mechanism.name: needs_houdini
marker_mechanism.applied_by: tests/conftest.py — pytest_collection_modifyitems(tryfirst=True). Auto-collected, never hand-applied. tests/conftest.py was EXTENDED (appended to), not replaced.
marker_mechanism.detection_rule: AST-based, module level ONLY. A module earns the marker if it has (1) an unguarded module-level `import hou` / `from pxr import ...`, (2) a module-level `pytest.importorskip("hou"|"pxr")`, or (3) a module-level `pytestmark = ...skipif(...)` whose source names the runtime.
marker_mechanism.why_ast_and_not_grep: The brief's grep `^\s*(import|from)\s+(hou|pxr)` reports 17 files. Only 7 of them actually hard-require a runtime. The grep's false positives are instructive: tests/test_e2e_tops.py:97 `import hou` is inside a STRING of code shipped over the wire; tests/test_marshal_hostile.py and tests/test_hou_reimport_guard.py import inside functions against the conftest's canonical FAKE hou and pass fine on a stock runner; tests/test_scene_memory.py and 5 others gate per-test, not per-module. Marking any of those would have deselected currently-passing tests — a green that lies by omission.

marked_set.note: The 3 pxr modules skip themselves at COLLECTION on a runner without pxr, so the marker never even reaches them there — they appear in the -rs skip block, not the deselect block. All 40 deselections in CI come from the 4 hou modules.

deliberately_not_marked.tests/test_usd_relationship_live.py: gated on $SYNAPSE_H22_LIVE, not on hou. 'needs a Houdini runtime' would be the wrong reason to show a reader.
deliberately_not_marked.tests/test_live_capture.py: its importorskip is nested inside a try, so it is not module level. It still skips itself, visibly.
deliberately_not_marked.tests/test_scene_memory.py + 5 others: gate per-test; most of their tests run and pass on a stock runner.

marker_mechanism.the_honesty_invariant: A module is marked ONLY IF it already refuses to run without its runtime on its own. The marker is therefore REDUNDANT with a gate the module already carries — everything the CI filter removes would have skipped anyway. It is structurally incapable of deselecting a test that would otherwise have run and passed.
marker_mechanism.invariant_is_enforced_not_asserted: tests/test_needs_houdini_marker.py, 18 tests: 5 positive detector controls, 7 negative detector controls (the dangerous direction — over-marking), the redundancy invariant itself, a real-hou-vs-fake-hou check, a 'the marker covers a nonempty set' check (a marker that marks nothing is a decoration that later gets cited as evidence), reason-string checks, and two workflow checks that fail if CI ever drops `not needs_houdini` or `-rs`.

measured_proof_that_nothing_is_hidden.reading: Identical collection, identical pass count. The 40 deselected come straight out of the 215 skipped (215 - 40 = 175). The filter changes SELECTION, never collection, and removes nothing that was passing.

visibility.skips: `-rs` added to the CI pytest step — prints every skip with its reason.
visibility.deselections: pytest prints NOTHING for -m deselections, which would have been a real silent hole. tests/conftest.py adds pytest_deselected + pytest_terminal_summary, so the CI summary carries a 'needs_houdini deselected (NOT silently dropped)' block naming each module, its test count, and the runtime it needs.
visibility.exact_reason_string_hou: needs a Houdini runtime: this module requires `hou` (Houdini's Python module -- exists only inside Houdini/hython, never on a stock interpreter)
visibility.exact_reason_string_pxr: needs a Houdini runtime: this module requires `pxr` (OpenUSD -- not installed on stock CI runners)

marker_mechanism.local_runs_unaffected: `pytest tests/` with no -m filter collects and runs everything, exactly as the receipts record. Verified: unfiltered 3.14 run is 5682 passed / 215 skipped / 0 deselected. The marker gates CI, not the developer.

findings.finding: `synapse_evolve_memory` / the `evolve_memory` command has been DEAD since 7f7bbc39 — ImportError on every call. Registered in _tool_registry.py:1070, routed in handlers.py:800, RBAC-listed in rbac.py:70, gated REVIEW in test_consent_timeout.py:59 — a fully wired tool with a broken import at the bottom. No test covered it, which is why CI never said so. The two failing tests WERE the only signal, pointing at it from one step away.

The first add() to any MonetaBackedStore force-saves synchronously, contradicting the module's own docstring at :162 ('deposit() writes to the in-memory ECS and returns immediately. There is no per-deposit fsync'). Measured, both directions — see B-1's probe table.

DOC DRIFT, not corrected here. The sentence 'Under the jsonl fallback, it still fires' is false — the module is retired, so evolution fires nowhere. CLAUDE.md §6 carries the same stale claim ('live only for the legacy jsonl path'). Both are governing/release documents; per Article VI a structural contradiction escalates rather than being silently amended, so they are recorded here for a human to correct (for_ruling #4).

The statusline reads `os.path.join(ROOT, '.git', 'HEAD')`. In a git LINKED WORKTREE `.git` is a 62-byte file, not a directory, so branch() returns '?' and head_sha() returns ''. Every agent worktree therefore shows a '?' branch, and 4 tests in tests/test_statusline.py fail there — in this worktree, at base, unrelated to any change. They pass in a real clone and on CI. Cost: any suite run inside a worktree reports 4 phantom failures, which is exactly the kind of noise that trains a reader to ignore red.

Three tests assert `elapsed > 0` against a clock whose granularity on Windows is ~15.6 ms, so a fast operation measures exactly 0.0. They fail on Windows + Python 3.11 AT THE BASE COMMIT (6 failed there vs 3 on 3.14), and the failing subset flickers between runs — 4 in one pass, 5 in the next — which is the flake signature. They passed on ubuntu-3.11 and macos-3.11 in the last completed green run (30772612918). Not caused by this leg, not fixed by it, and not marked needs_houdini (they have nothing to do with Houdini).

BRIEF DRIFT, benign. The brief states '23 of 310 test files import hou or pxr directly'. The grep it names returns 17 files across 309 test files, and only 7 of those hard-require a runtime; the rest already guard themselves. Following the stated number literally would have deselected ~10 modules' worth of currently-passing tests. The brief's own ruling (honesty over a green badge) outranks its own premise, so the marked set was derived from the tree instead.

for_ruling.question: Should MonetaBackedStore keep force-saving the FIRST deposit?
for_ruling.context: `_last_save = 0.0` (moneta_store.py:205) makes add()'s periodic-save check always true on the first deposit. Two defensible readings, and this is a durability-posture call, not a fact.
for_ruling.option_a: KEEP IT (what this leg did). No production behaviour change; the first deposit survives a kill -9. Cost: the module docstring's 'there is no per-deposit fsync' stays false for deposit #1, and the tests have to carry the boundary explanation.
for_ruling.option_b: SET `_last_save = time.monotonic()` in __init__. One line. Probed: the ORIGINAL single-deposit assertions then pass verbatim. Makes the docstring true and the timer mean what it says. Cost: a lone deposit followed by kill -9 within 30 s is now lost — which the docstring already documents as the bound, but it is still a real reduction.
for_ruling.why_escalated: Article I — a value judgement between defensible options, and a CI-greening leg is the wrong place to quietly change durability semantics.

for_ruling.question: Should `synapse_evolve_memory` stay a registered tool at all?
for_ruling.context: F1: it was dead since 7f7bbc39 and nobody noticed, which is evidence about how much it is used. This leg rerouted it to shared/evolution.py::LosslessEvolution so it works again. The alternative is deprecating the tool outright, since Moneta consolidation (`sleep_pass`) supersedes markdown->USD evolution.
for_ruling.why_escalated: What to deprecate is explicitly a human call (Article I).

for_ruling.question: Fix the three zero-elapsed-time assertions (F5), or leave them?
for_ruling.context: They only fail on Windows dev machines, never on the ubuntu/macos legs CI runs. A real fix means `time.perf_counter()` in the routing/session product code; changing `> 0` to `>= 0` would be weakening a test and was not done.
for_ruling.why_escalated: Out of this leg's scope, and it touches product timing code in two subsystems.

for_ruling.question: Correct the two stale evolution sentences (F3)?
for_ruling.context: docs/DEBUT_READINESS.md:122 and CLAUDE.md §6 both still say evolution fires under the jsonl path. It fires nowhere. Both are governing/release documents.
for_ruling.why_escalated: Article VI — an agent does not silently amend a governing document, even to correct a fact.

for_ruling.question: Make harness/statusline.py worktree-aware (F4)?
for_ruling.context: Every agent worktree shows a '?' branch and 4 red statusline tests. The fix is reading the `gitdir:` pointer when `.git` is a file. Small, but it is the bar's own design and the bar was built to be subprocess-free under 100 ms.
for_ruling.why_escalated: Not this leg's surface; the tests it breaks are green on CI.
